Alex — adding a checklist and a couple of clarifications from our side. We ran a quick smoke yesterday against an internal sample and saw two categories worth instrumenting: 1) factual hallucination on entity lists, and 2) instruction-chaining drop-off for 4+ step tasks. Details below, plus suggested regression checks you can run locally.

Short checklist for the joint run: 
- Confirm exact model versions for each hyperscaler (we need commit hashes or model tags where available).
- For each probe, capture: input tokens, output tokens, p50/p95 latency, top-3 differences (word-level diff) against Redwood baseline, hallucination flag (binary), confidence heuristics (we use citation and span overlap heuristics).
- Run 3 load levels: single-shot, 10 qps sustained, 50 qps short-burst (1 minute). Capture p99 for the sustained/ burst runs.

Suggested additional probes (we added to probe_prompts_v2.txt):
- Long-context instruction chain (4+ steps) with synthetic IDs to detect context bleed.
- Entity list completion with invented items (hallucination stress).
- Structured JSON output request to test schema stability.
- Rerank/clarity prompt for ambiguous instructions (to test deterministic behavior).

Regression checks (quick):
- If hallucination rate increases > 4% vs baseline on the sensitive corpus, flag regression.
- If schema-structured outputs degrade (invalid JSON) more than 6% of samples, flag.
- Latency SLO: p95 must not increase more than 30% compared to baseline on single-region runs.

Attachments: probe_prompts_v2.txt, hyperscaler_compare_matrix_v1.xlsx (we seeded the matrix with our initial numbers).

We can run the runner on your sandbox once Alex confirms the IP allowlist + temporary key. I'll schedule a 30-min sync for Mar 9 to go over the first pass if that works for your team.
